_meta.anthropic/searchHint: scroll wheel list page chromium mouse down up content fold

description:
Scroll content in a Chromium app by dispatching mouse-wheel events at a point. Anchor x/y are normalized 0.0–1.0 (fractions of the window, not pixels), same coordinate space as gesture-tap and describe. Deltas are fractions of the window too: deltaY 0.5 scrolls down half a window; negative scrolls back up.
Use when content is below/above the fold (describe shows off-screen elements with zero height) or a list needs scrolling. Chromium only — on iOS/Android use gesture-swipe.
Returns { scrolled: true, timestampMs }. Fails if the Chromium CDP session is not reachable for the given device.

deltaX.description: Horizontal scroll distance as a fraction of the window width (e.g. 0.5 = half a window). Positive scrolls content right (reveals content to the right).

deltaY.description: Vertical scroll distance as a fraction of the window height (e.g. 0.5 = half a window). Positive scrolls content down (reveals content below), like rolling a mouse wheel toward you.

durationMs.description: Spread the scroll over this many milliseconds in wheel-event steps (default 300) so scroll handlers fire progressively.

x.description: Anchor x: normalized 0.0–1.0 (fraction of window width, not pixels). The wheel events land here — put it over the element you want to scroll.

y.description: Anchor y: normalized 0.0–1.0 (fraction of window height, not pixels).

name: gesture-scroll
